data.description:
Produce a personal debrief and game plan. Generates "today", "rest of this week", and "past 7 days recap" sections by pulling from Google Calendar, Gmail, Notion, vmem memories/wiki, and recent chats. Use when user asks "what should I do today", "catch me up", "weekly review", "debrief me", "what did I do this week", or invokes /debrief.
argument-hint: "Optional focus filter (e.g. 'just work', 'personal only', project name)"
data.instructions:
Generate a personal debrief covering three windows: **today**, **rest of this week**, and **past 7 days**. The user invokes this to orient themselves at the start of a day, before a meeting, or after a break.

## Pull data in parallel

Query all of these in one batch before writing anything:

- **Google Calendar** — events for today and through end of Sunday. Note times, attendees, locations, which are anchor commitments vs skippable.
- **Gmail** — threads from the last 7 days; flag anything awaiting the user's reply.
- **Notion** — recently updated pages; look for task lists, planning docs, project trackers.
- **vmem memory_search** with no query (recent first) and **memory_retrieve** for project keywords — episodic memories from the last 7 days; profile facts and pinned knowledge that frame priorities.
- **vmem wiki_list / wiki_search** — current project docs and todo-style pages.
- **conversation_search / recent_chats** — past chats from the last 7 days for technical work and decisions.
- **vmem codebases_list** — only if the user mentions code work; otherwise skip.

If a source is empty, errors, or isn't connected, note it briefly under "gaps" at the end — don't fabricate substitutes.

## Synthesize

Write three short sections. Be specific — name the meeting, the PR, the doc, the person. Vague debriefs are useless.

### Today
- 1–3 anchor commitments (calendar events that can't move)
- 1–3 focus tasks (what would make today a win)
- Anything time-sensitive (replies owed today, deadlines)

### Rest of the week
- Major calendar items grouped by day
- Project milestones or deadlines landing this week
- Decisions or follow-ups due before the week ends

### Past week recap
- 3–7 bullets of what actually got done (shipped code, decisions made, meetings held, docs written)
- Group by project/theme, not by day
- Call out anything left half-done or blocked

## Optional sections (include only if non-trivial)

- **Loose ends** — emails awaiting reply, items dropped, follow-ups owed
- **Suggested first move** — one sentence answering "what should I do in the next 30 minutes?"
- **Gaps** — sources that were empty or unreachable

## Format

- Bullets, not paragraphs. The whole thing should be scannable in under a minute.
- Lead with Today. No preamble like "Here's your debrief!" — start with the heading.
- If the user passed an argument, treat it as a focus filter (e.g. "just work" → drop personal items; "carepulse" → narrow to that project).

## Don't

- Don't list every calendar event — filter to what matters.
- Don't pad the recap with trivial events to hit a count.
- Don't recommend actions you can't ground in the pulled data.
- Don't query sources sequentially when parallel works.
- Don't include "completed" items you only inferred; if a memory or chat shows work-in-progress, say so.

data.description:
Produce a personal debrief and game plan. Generates "today", "rest of this week", and "past 7 days recap" sections by pulling from Google Calendar, Gmail, Notion, vmem memories/wiki, and recent chats. Use when user asks "what should I do today", "catch me up", "weekly review", "debrief me", "what did I do this week", or invokes /debrief.
argument-hint: "Optional focus filter (e.g. 'just work', 'personal only', project name)"
data.instructions:
Generate a personal debrief covering three windows: **today**, **rest of this week**, and **past 7 days**. The user invokes this to orient themselves at the start of a day, before a meeting, or after a break.

## Pull data in parallel

Query all of these in one batch before writing anything:

- **Google Calendar** — events for today and through end of Sunday. Note times, attendees, locations, which are anchor commitments vs skippable.
- **Gmail** — threads from the last 7 days; flag anything awaiting the user's reply.
- **Notion** — recently updated pages; look for task lists, planning docs, project trackers.
- **vmem memory_search** with no query (recent first) and **memory_retrieve** for project keywords — episodic memories from the last 7 days; profile facts and pinned knowledge that frame priorities.
- **vmem wiki_list / wiki_search** — current project docs and todo-style pages.
- **conversation_search / recent_chats** — past chats from the last 7 days for technical work and decisions.
- **vmem codebases_list** — only if the user mentions code work; otherwise skip.

If a source is empty, errors, or isn't connected, note it briefly under "gaps" at the end — don't fabricate substitutes.

## Synthesize

Write three short sections. Be specific — name the meeting, the PR, the doc, the person. Vague debriefs are useless.

### Today
- 1–3 anchor commitments (calendar events that can't move)
- 1–3 focus tasks (what would make today a win)
- Anything time-sensitive (replies owed today, deadlines)

### Rest of the week
- Major calendar items grouped by day
- Project milestones or deadlines landing this week
- Decisions or follow-ups due before the week ends

### Past week recap
- 3–7 bullets of what actually got done (shipped code, decisions made, meetings held, docs written)
- Group by project/theme, not by day
- Call out anything left half-done or blocked

## Optional sections (include only if non-trivial)

- **Loose ends** — emails awaiting reply, items dropped, follow-ups owed
- **Suggested first move** — one sentence answering "what should I do in the next 30 minutes?"
- **Gaps** — sources that were empty or unreachable

## Format

- Bullets, not paragraphs. The whole thing should be scannable in under a minute.
- Lead with Today. No preamble like "Here's your debrief!" — start with the heading.
- If the user passed an argument, treat it as a focus filter (e.g. "just work" → drop personal items; "carepulse" → narrow to that project).

## Don't

- Don't list every calendar event — filter to what matters.
- Don't pad the recap with trivial events to hit a count.
- Don't recommend actions you can't ground in the pulled data.
- Don't query sources sequentially when parallel works.
- Don't include "completed" items you only inferred; if a memory or chat shows work-in-progress, say so.
